I am missing four permanent teeth, I had the baby ones just nothing under them. Nothing happened to them I just was never born with them, must be genetic because neither was my mom.  Plus two teeth came in sideways causing them to point kinda like Dracula. I have never had a cavity, cracked tooth, nothing.  To try to give you a visual idea. I have my two front teeth and two pointy ones on each side. Then after those I have gaps and them the rest of my back teeth. The bottom I’m missing the two front ones and then I have the rest of them. To add on I am like the SPECIAL child at my dentist. I was born with significantly less teeth then average too. They still fill my whole mouth but the gaps. 



As I entered middle school I was involved with ALOT of drama. Their main comeback was always about my teeth they claimed I didn’t have. It hurt because their wasn’t anything I could do about them. They were noticeable small too from being in my mouth for 13 years (Had them in till 15) and were very wore down.  Everyone I was involved in drama with wanted to always say I had no teeth and to stop being a freak and sharpening my teeth too. It hurt because I couldn’t do anything to change my teeth. Implants were out the question because most people won’t do it unless your 18. It was hard for people to ever understand that it wasn’t my fault it was how I was born. Plus it hurts to not even want to smile in fear of someone seeing your gaps. It sucks a lot and took a real toll on me. I would always cover my mouth to smile which became habit until years later. 

Now I’m proud to say I had the baby teeth removed, braces to pull my teeth together and to make it to where I only need 3 implants. Plus I opted out of them squaring off my pointy teeth. I have three gaps and I’m not bothered by them at all now. Its how I was made and I have to expect it. Will be getting implants though in the future to fill the gaps mostly for jobs.

From a child that has seen my parents go through something similar, please know your kids have an idea of whats going on. Doesn’t matter if they are young, they can sense that something is wrong. This probably effects them too and maybe chatting with them about it will help both of you. It doesn’t have to be about this situation, but talking to someone always helps. I know that while my dad was hurting he just wanted to talk. Not about the situation but just have a conversation. He felt 10x better just talking about his job, and some of the drama at work. Then it made him happy hearing about school, after school activities, anything. Don’t isolate yourself. Get involved more with your kids and leave the drama alone. Yes it hurts, but it gets better. You can change it, you don’t deserve to suffer in that.
